text:
The Lake Wind Advisory is up, so keep tonight’s waterfront plans close to shore. For Burlington, sunset at 7:08 looks dry with a mostly clear sky still holding, though the south wind will be gusty, then clouds thicken overnight. Showers become likely after 1am, with a low around 62 and gusts up to 30 mph. On the lake, waves build to 3 to 5 feet, so this is not a good night for a small boat.

Sunday starts gray with a chance of showers, then the afternoon stays unsettled, with more showers and a slight chance of thunderstorms. The high should land near 78, but the guidance ranges from the mid 70s to near 80, and the rain odds run from roughly two-thirds to nearly certain. Winds remain strong early, easing later. Enjoy the sunset, but be off the water before dark and keep outdoor plans flexible after breakfast tomorrow.

week.blurb: Sunny and breezy, near 77, then showers arrive after 1am; make daytime plans, but keep rain gear handy overnight.
Showers and a few thunderstorms could interrupt Sunday, with a mostly cloudy high near 78 and rain likely again overnight.
Mostly sunny and cooler Monday near 67, though a stray shower remains possible; the forecast is drier than some models suggest.
Mostly sunny Tuesday, near 71, with dry daytime plans favored before a slight shower chance arrives after 2am.
Partly sunny and warm near 77 Wednesday, with only a slight shower chance early and again after 2am.
Thursday looks warm near 77, but showers are likely through the day and into the night despite some sun.
A cooler Friday near 72, partly sunny after a few morning showers; the night turns partly cloudy and calmer.
